questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to become a faster swimmer in just a few weeks
Safety rules for young children at the local pool
Good manners and unwritten rules in swimming pools
Why swimming is good for your health and your mood
questions.why: Neil explains 'wetiquette' means swimming pool etiquette: dos and don'ts to keep things calm in the water.

questions.q: Why does Neil think everyone should shower before swimming?
options: Because it's the law in the UK for all public pools
It's easy and keeps sweat and bacteria out of the pool
It helps you swim faster because your skin is smoother
It warms your body up before you get into the cold water
questions.why: Neil says a shower is easy and stops 'horrible sweat and bacteria' getting in the pool.

questions.q: According to Jenny Landreth, what causes 'lane rage'?
options: People running beside the pool
Too many swimmers in the pool at once
Swimmers diving in the shallow end
People being in the wrong lane for their speed
questions.why: She says most swimmers suffer lane rage if people are in the wrong lane of the pool.

questions.q: Who does Jenny say often misjudges their speed?
options: Men
Children
Older women
New swimmers
questions.why: She says 'gentlemen quite often misjudge their speed' and think they're faster than they are.

questions.q: Why do these swimmers often choose a faster lane, according to Jenny?
options: The slow lane is usually too crowded at lunchtime
They are training for races and need more space
They don't know which lane is which because of bad signs
They don't like a woman swimming faster than them
questions.why: Jenny says they often don't like it if a woman is swimming faster than them.

questions.q: What does it mean if someone taps your foot in the pool?
options: They want you to stop swimming
They want to pass you
You are in the wrong lane
They are asking for help
questions.why: Neil says if somebody taps your foot, it means they want to overtake you.

questions.q: What is Rob suggesting when he asks if it's Neil's 'male ego talking'?
options: Neil may be like the men who hate being beaten
Neil is a very slow swimmer and should practise more
Neil should swim in the fast lane with the other men
Neil is scared of the water and can't swim well
questions.why: Neil says he hates being overtaken, and Rob links this to the male ego Jenny described.

questions.q: What reason does Neil give for hating being overtaken?
options: It makes him feel slow
It is against the pool rules
He doesn't like getting splashed
It makes him lose count of his lengths
questions.why: Neil says 'No, not at all – I just hate getting splashed'.
